title: Add a routine to report rename failures.
description:
Take the routine from file.c, move it to ui/alert_box.c, and give it
both an old file name and a new file name argument.

notes.body: enabled an automatic merge when all merge checks for 5774d3513ab148af5a77b038f6cf4c55691fe297 pass

@guyharris 

I cannot build anymore:

```
/home/eugene/wireshark/ui/alert_box.c: In function ‘rename_failure_alert_box’:
/home/eugene/wireshark/ui/alert_box.c:618:10: error: ‘ENOENT’ undeclared (first use in this function)
  618 |     case ENOENT:
```


However including errno seems to solve:

```
--- a/ui/alert_box.c
+++ b/ui/alert_box.c
@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@
 #include "config.h"
 
 #include <string.h>
+#include <errno.h>
```

On what platform were you building this?  I'm guessing the reason it didn't show up on any of the platforms the GitLab builders are using is that, on those platforms, either 1) some other system header file we're including happens to {transitive-closure-of-include} <errno.h> or 2) some #ifdef in one of our headers {transitive-closure-of-included} by that source file causes <errno.h> to be included.

On Linux Mint 20, the About dialog gives this below.
I had other problems recently related to the Qt version but John fixed them.

```
Compiled (64-bit) using GCC 9.4.0, with GLib 2.64.3, with Qt 5.12.8, with libpcap, without POSIX capabilities, without libnl, with zlib 1.2.11, without zlib-ng, with PCRE2, without Lua, without GnuTLS, with Gcrypt 1.8.5, without Kerberos, without MaxMind, with nghttp2 1.40.0, without nghttp3, without brotli, without LZ4, with Zstandard, without Snappy, without libxml2, without libsmi, without Minizip, with QtMultimedia, with QtDBus, without automatic updates, with binary plugins, debug build. 
Running on Linux 5.4.0-26-generic, with Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700HQ CPU @ 2.60GHz (with SSE4.2), with 7934 MB of physical memory, with GLib 2.64.3, with Qt 5.12.8, with libpcap 1.9.1 (with TPACKET_V3), with zlib 1.2.11, with PCRE2 10.34 2019-11-21, with c-ares 1.15.0, with Gcrypt 1.8.5, with nghttp2 1.40.0, with Zstandard 1.4.4, with light display mode, without HiDPI, with Xorg, with QPA plugin "xcb", with LC_TYPE=en_US.UTF-8, binary plugins supported. 
```

At least according to [the Linux Mint Wikipedia page's "Releases" section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_Mint#Releases), Linux Mint 20 is based on Ubuntu 20; I have an Ubuntu 20.04 VM on which I'll try a build without the <errno.h>.  Perhaps some GNU libc header differs between the GNU libc versions in those versions and whatever version of Ubuntu is running on our Ubuntu GitLab builder.

Yes it's based on Ubuntu 20.04 but honestly I don't know what are the differences in terms of libraries (the user desktop is quite different and more comfortable in my opinion). If I have to test anything, just ask.

> I have an Ubuntu 20.04 VM on which I'll try a build without the <errno.h>.

Yes, it fails to compile on Ubuntu 20.04 as well. Probably nothing short of testing with several versions of several Linux distributions, several versions of all the major \*BSDs, several versions of macOS with several versions of Xcode, several versions of Windows, and several versions of HP-UX/AIX/Solaris, with, on each platform, several versions of all C/C++ compilers for that platform - and all done with a variety of configuration options - will come close to fully catching all build breakages.

Ubuntu 20.04 and RHEL 8, and their respective derivatives, are just about the oldest distributions that currently build with the master branch. Neither of them are currently in CI, and we seem to break them a lot on the master branch.

In the case of Ubuntu 20.04, it is going out of support in April 2025 (and Mint 20 shortly thereafter), at least for the normal non paid support. It's fairly unlikely we will have a new release branch before then, so personally I am inclined to boost the minimum Qt requirement to 5.15 (5.12 is well out of support by the Qt Company) and drop Ubuntu 20 based support, leaving it to 4.4

That doesn't deal with the issue of trying to avoid breaking 4.4 or earlier on Ubuntu 20, though.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -123,6 +123,17 @@ extern void read_failure_alert_box(const char *filename, int err);
  */
 extern void write_failure_alert_box(const char *filename, int err);
 
+/*
+ * Alert box for a failed attempt to rename a file.
+ * "err" is assumed to be a UNIX-style errno.
+ *
+ * XXX - whether we mention the source pathname, the target pathname,
+ * or both depends on the error and on what we find if we look for
+ * one or both of them.
+ */
+extern void rename_failure_alert_box(const char *old_filename,
+                                     const char *new_filename, int err);
+
 #ifdef __cplusplus
 }
 #endif /* __cplusplus */
